parts.text: A flowerpot saucer, clogged gutter, discarded tire, birdbath or even a bottle cap can collect enough water for mosquito

to develop. A single Aedes aegypti mosquito can lay more than 100 eggs at a time up to five times during its lifespan, which is only about a month.

As suburban neighborhoods expand, so do opportunities for mosquitoes to breed and find humans for their

.

Across the United States, new housing developments create thousands of these small water-holding containers and bring together the two things these mosquitoes need: standing water and people.

This combination allows them to spread through

networks, establishing populations far from their original ranges, and explains why mosquito expansion is often linked to patterns of human movement and development.

Aedes albopictus, originally native to Southeast Asia and now found in all habitable

, provides a striking example of this spread. These mosquitoes arrived in the U.S. mostly because of human actions. They stowed away on boats and other vehicles, often riding in used tires or lucky bamboo.

Their early dispersal in the U.S. has been linked to the

highway system. By 2017, Aedes albopictus was documented in 1,368 counties across 40 states, and it has continued to expand across much of the eastern and central U.S.

One of Iowa’s first established Aedes albopictus populations, for example, appeared in the Des Moines

area, where it has continued to grow and expand to other communities.

Its spread from southeast Asia all the way to the U.S. Midwest demonstrates how

and suburban growth can create opportunities for mosquitoes.

US’s most common mosquito threat: West Nile

West Nile virus remains the most widespread mosquito-borne disease in the continental United States. It is primarily transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, including common house mosquitoes, which are found in much of the country.

Culex mosquitoes can breed in a wide range of
, including storm drains, roadside ditches, retention ponds, wetlands and other standing water. Their ability to thrive in both urban and rural environments has helped make West Nile virus an

public health concern in many states.

Because Culex mosquitoes are already established across much of the country, climate change may not necessarily introduce them to new regions. Instead, research is increasingly focused on how changing
and precipitation patterns could influence their abundance, seasonal activity and ability to transmit disease.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Human development creates opportunities for mosquitoes and the diseases they transmit.
Comparing Scotland and Wales reveals policy choices that influence recycling performance.
New tracking technologies are changing knowledge of bird migration and opportunities for conservation.
Dry climates can increase river nitrate pollution even far from intensive human activity.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Rising global temperatures and shorter winters expand the area suitable for mosquitoes to live in and transmit viruses that cause diseases.

questions.prompt: What is identified as one reason mosquitoes are becoming more common in some places?
options: The disappearance of every source of standing water
The complete absence of human development
A universal decline in temperature everywhere
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Climate change is part of the reason people in many parts of the country are seeing more mosquitoes.
